q: A primary purpose of establishing a supervision contract at the outset is to:
choices: A. Guarantee that the supervisee will pass the certification exam on schedule
B. Specify the mutual expectations and responsibilities of both parties
C. Replace the need for ongoing performance feedback and direct observation
D. Transfer ethical accountability for services to the supervisee

q: A discriminative stimulus (SD) is defined as a stimulus in the presence of which:
choices: A. Behavior is physically incompatible with any competing response
B. Behavior has been punished and is therefore less probable
C. Behavior is reinforced on a fixed-interval schedule of delivery
D. Behavior has been reinforced and is therefore more probable

q: Asked “What do you drink?”, a learner names the beverage he has been deprived of all morning. This reflects:
choices: A. Audience control exerted by the instructor asking the question
B. A formal prompt sharing point-to-point correspondence with the response
C. Failure of stimulus generalization across settings and instructors
D. A motivating operation exerting mand control over an intraverbal

q: Self-management programs often require external support early on because:
choices: A. The controlled response cannot be measured without an outside observer
B. Reactivity from self-recording always shifts behavior the wrong way
C. Antecedent manipulation is ineffective when applied to one's own behavior
D. The controlling response is itself behavior that must be reinforced

q: The critical difference between operant and respondent conditioning is that operant conditioning:
choices: A. Involves responses elicited by an antecedent conditioned stimulus
B. Requires an unconditioned stimulus to be paired with a neutral stimulus
C. Applies only to reflexive responses in non-human organisms
D. Is governed by consequences of behavior rather than stimulus pairing

q: The primary advantage of functional analysis over descriptive assessment for function identification is that FA:
choices: A. Is faster and far less resource-intensive than descriptive methods
B. Can be designed and interpreted by RBTs without BCBA oversight
C. Does not require the behavior to occur during the assessment
D. Establishes causation by experimentally manipulating variables

q: A client begins screaming and refusing food within one week, with no change to programming, staff, or setting. The BCBA should first:
choices: A. Recommend medical evaluation before further assessment
B. Increase reinforcement density during mealtime demands
C. Implement escape extinction across all mealtime sessions
D. Begin a functional analysis of the mealtime refusal behavior

q: Occurrence and non-occurrence IOA are reported separately primarily because:
choices: A. Non-occurrence agreement is always lower than occurrence agreement
B. The BACB requires the split for legal defensibility of agency records
C. Overall IOA can look acceptable while occurrence agreement is poor
D. Overall IOA cannot be calculated for interval-recording data

q: Which question best distinguishes a discriminative stimulus from a motivating operation?
choices: A. Was the consequence ever unavailable without the antecedent?
B. Does the antecedent increase the frequency of the behavior?
C. Is the antecedent a person, an object, or a spoken instruction?
D. Does the antecedent reliably precede the behavior in time?

q: The 'least restrictive alternative' principle in the BACB Ethics Code requires that behavior analysts:
choices: A. Obtain written consent before implementing any behavior plan
B. Use the least restrictive of comparably effective interventions
C. Avoid all punishment-based procedures under every circumstance
D. Always choose the least restrictive option regardless of effectiveness

q: A response class is defined by:
choices: A. Responses that occur within the same observation interval
B. Responses evoked by the same antecedent stimulus
C. Topographical similarity among the responses in the set
D. Responses producing the same effect on the environment

q: A behavioral cusp is best defined as a behavior change that:
choices: A. Exposes the person to new environments and contingencies
B. Must be reinforced on a continuous schedule to maintain
C. Reduces problem behavior to a socially acceptable rate
D. Can be acquired only through massed discrete-trial teaching

q: According to Kazdin (1977), vague operational definitions most directly contribute to:
choices: A. Overestimation of behavior by partial-interval recording
B. Ratio strain when a reinforcement schedule is thinned quickly
C. Reduced inter-observer agreement from inconsistent scoring
D. Extinction bursts during the first treatment sessions

q: Resurgence refers to:
choices: A. Reappearance of extinguished behavior after a period of non-exposure
B. An increase in problem behavior following reinforcement schedule thinning
C. Return of an extinguished behavior when a newer response is extinguished
D. The temporary rate increase seen when extinction is first implemented

q: An RBT has run a DRA plan for three weeks with no change in problem behavior. The BCBA should first:
choices: A. Add a punishment component to the existing plan
B. Conclude the function hypothesis was wrong and reassess
C. Collect procedural integrity data on the DRA plan
D. Increase the magnitude of the alternative reinforcer

q: Which consequence of unethical practice falls at the level of risk to the profession?
choices: A. Revocation of an individual practitioner's BACB certification
B. A civil suit filed against the individual practitioner
C. A client losing a developmental window to ineffective care
D. Funders restricting coverage for behavior-analytic services

q: A behavior analyst may disclose confidential client information without specific client consent when:
choices: A. The information would make an interesting social media post
B. Another professional requests the file out of general interest
C. Disclosure is required by law, as in mandated abuse reporting
D. A colleague casually asks how a recognizable case is going

q: In a typical RIRD procedure for vocal stereotypy, redirection continues until the individual:
choices: A. Has been ignored for a fixed interval of sixty seconds
B. Emits a number of appropriate responses without stereotypy
C. Is placed in a brief exclusionary timeout from the activity
D. Receives a preferred edible for a sustained period of silence

q: Extinguished attention-maintained disruption returns immediately after a visitor spontaneously hugs the client mid-session. The mechanism is:
choices: A. Resurgence produced by extinction of the alternative
B. Spontaneous recovery after the passage of time
C. Reinstatement from a free delivery of the reinforcer
D. Renewal produced by a change in the treatment context

q: A behavior analyst is asked to design a language intervention for a client with complex AAC needs who has had no prior SLP involvement. The most appropriate course of action is:
choices: A. Decline the case entirely and refer the client elsewhere
B. Collaborate with a speech-language pathologist on the AAC system
C. Conduct a verbal behavior assessment and proceed independently
D. Implement a verbal behavior program using the BCBA's own training

q: An undifferentiated functional analysis outcome (similar responding across all conditions, including control) should lead the analyst to:
choices: A. Conclude the behavior has no function and discontinue assessment
B. Immediately implement a punishment-based reduction plan
C. Conclude the behavior is maintained by attention by default
D. Modify the analysis and repeat it before drawing conclusions
